html:
The Weenhayek are the Bolivian branch of the Wichí people, living along the Pilcomayo River in the Gran Chaco of Tarija department, near the town of Villa Montes.

Their life has long centred on the river. They fish the great runs of sábalo that come up the Pilcomayo each year, and they gather and hunt in the dry forest. The Chaco War between Bolivia and Paraguay in the 1930s was fought around them, and Bolivian settlers and ranchers then took much of their land. Bolivia granted them a land title in the 1990s. Their language is the westernmost variety of Wichí. Like other lowland peoples they gained new rights in the Plurinational State of Bolivia.
sum: The Weenhayek are the Bolivian branch of the Wichí people, living along the Pilcomayo River in the Gran Chaco of Tarija department, near the town of Villa Montes.
